cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: probability of exactly 6 successes in 10 trials at p=0.5
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.2050781. Independently derived from the documented probability mass function COMBIN(n,x)*p^x*(1-p)^(n-x): C(10,6)*0.5^10 = 210/1024 = 0.205078125 exactly -> 0.2050781 at 7 dp

cases.description: The same parameters with cumulative TRUE, giving the probability of at most 6 successes
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that with cumulative TRUE the function returns "the probability that there are at most number_s successes", i.e. the sum of the mass function for k = 0..6. Independently derived: (C(10,0)+...+C(10,6))/1024 = (1+10+45+120+210+252+210)/1024 = 848/1024 = 0.828125 exactly

cases.description: Non-integer number_s and trials, which the documentation says are truncated
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "Number_s and trials are truncated to integers", so 6.9 and 10.9 must behave exactly as 6 and 10 and return the documented 0.205078125. Independently checked that a genuine non-truncating evaluation would differ: with 7 successes in 11 trials the mass is C(11,7)*0.5^11 = 330/2048 = 0.161133
Excel documents: "If number_s < 0 or number_s > trials, BINOM.DIST returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If probability_s < 0 or probability_s > 1, BINOM.DIST returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If number_s, trials, or probability_s is nonnumeric, BINOM.DIST returns the #VALUE! error value."
